integrity.notes: doit.py test-integrity TASK-3.13 exits 0. The product diff is a named constant, a total switch over Speed, and the hook's bot setTimeout now reads botActionDelayMs(table.config.speed). It does not recognise test inputs, hard-code expected values, take early exits, mock the unit under test or override equality. The test-only pace worker and harness are imported only from e2e/; after `npm run build`, grep of dist for tlh-test-pace-advice / Pace harness / TlhPaceHarness finds nothing.

items.evidence: tests/table/pace.test.ts passes and asserts RAPID_BOT_DELAY_MS === 0 and botActionDelayMs('rapid') === 0. The mutation to 400 makes it fail. Holdout model check via the public session API: constant 0, botActionDelayMs('rapid') 0, and the default, empty and sit-and-go configs all resolve to speed 'rapid' with a 0 ms delay → OK.

Both paused-clock tests pass in chromium and webkit (every-push run and slow run). The guard can fail: the 400 ms mutant meters 101 ms against the 100 ms cap in both projects. The recorded cap+1 deviation is correct, because returning exactly cap would let a stuck action pass <= cap. The same-origin request assertion is present. Holdout, real app in both engines: the page schedules only 0 ms and 1500 ms timers across 3 hands; 24 bot gaps, max 17 ms; the only request origin is localhost:4173.

The model test passes in 79 ms. It asserts 200 hands, every delay 1500, scheduled === 300000, botActions > 0, worst case < 1 h and >= 200 hands/h. The mutant fails it (871600 != 300000). Holdout with 3 other replay seeds: 200 hands, scheduled 300000, about 1385-1446 bot actions, worst case 715500-733800 ms (981-1006 hands/h). The held hand returns null delay.
e2e:slow chromium: 80 samples, max 17.7 ms <= 300; skip reason and Chromium-only gating present. Holdout real-time 6-max with a different pinned seed: max bot gap 17.2 ms (chromium), 3.0 ms (webkit).

e2e:slow chromium: 235 samples, max 50.3 ms <= 300; header assertion 'Cash · 10 players · $4/$8 · Hand #1' present. The recorded deviation is acceptable on substance. Bot decisions come from a test-only raise-first worker (the 6-max chart throws at 10 seats until TASK-7.6), but the requests go through the production path: useTableSession → botActionDelayMs → shared advice client → worker host. TASK-7.6 AC#10 carries the re-proof with real TAG bots. Holdout 10-max harness, different seed: header correct, 10 seats, the user folds, 47 bot gaps with max 40.4 ms, and only 0/1500 ms timers are scheduled. Under the 400 ms mutant the same holdout fails, which shows the harness exercises the production delay.

e2e:slow chromium: 200 hands, elapsedMs 368510 (>= 300000 and < 3600000), 1953.8 hands/h; 65 min timeout set. The scripted user waits 1.5 s before clicking Deal next hand when held, and the run stops at Hand #201.
